_comment: Manual resolutions for dataset cities the gazetteer matcher cannot resolve on its own.
Keys are dataset record ids (city--state). A value is either { geoid } pointing at a row
in the places gazetteer, or { lat, lon } for a place the places file does not contain.
The build FAILS listing every unresolved city, so this file cannot drift out of date.
Every entry needs a 'why' — no silent guesses.

athens--ga.why: Consolidated city-county; the gazetteer name is 'Athens-Clarke County unified government (balance)'.

boise--id.why: The city's legal name is 'Boise City'; the survey uses the everyday name 'Boise'.

nashville--tn.why: Consolidated city-county; the gazetteer name is 'Nashville-Davidson metropolitan government (balance)'.

new-gloucester--me.why: Maine towns are county subdivisions, not Census 'places'. Coordinates are the internal point of 'New Gloucester town' (GEOID 2300548820) from the 2025 county-subdivision gazetteer.
new-gloucester--me.confirm: This city also has no region or population_size in the survey file.

oakwood--oh.why: Ohio has three Oakwoods. Picked Oakwood city in Montgomery County (Dayton area, ~9,500 residents) over the two much smaller villages in Cuyahoga and Paulding counties.
oakwood--oh.confirm: All three are under 10,000, so the survey's population bucket does not disambiguate. Worth confirming with NLC which Oakwood responded.
